args.title: aca-redline.docx
args.body:
ACCOUNT CONTROL AGREEMENT — TRACKED-CHANGES REDLINE
Northgale Systems, Inc. (as Secured Party) / Corvid Analytics LLC (as Debtor) / [Depository Bank]
Redline of counterparty rev draft against internal commercial contracting playbook (2026 ed.), executed credit agreement, depository bank standard form, account details, and deal correspondence.

PRELIMINARY NOTE. This redline reconciles the counterparty's draft markup against (i) the internal playbook's Standard positions and Fallbacks, (ii) the executed credit agreement, (iii) the depository bank's standard-form Account Control Agreement, (iv) the account details schedule, and (v) the controlling deal-correspondence instruction of 21 July 2026 (the supplemental instruction letter). Per the controlling instruction: the client CONCEDES the indemnification-basket conversion (deductible → tipping), but treats ANY survival-period reduction as a walk-away issue. The scheduled exceptions (Schedule 3.7, Schedule 5.2, Exhibit B) qualify the general provisions and CONTROL. The unrelated administrative file 6 correspondence is excluded from reliance.

The redline below shows, provision by provision, the base/firm-standard language (bracketed, with deletions shown by strikethrough), the counterparty's markup (shown by underline-and-shading annotations as introduced), and the required post-redline text (indicated by the operative instruction). Tracked changes are represented as [BASE TEXT] → [REQUIRED TEXT], with the counter-draft edits marked.

=====================================================================
SECTION 1 — DEFINITIONS
=====================================================================

1.1 "Material Adverse Effect"
Base (playbook Standard / depository bank standard form): "Material Adverse Effect" means any event, change, condition, occurrence or effect that, individually or in the aggregate, has a material adverse effect on the business, condition (financial or otherwise), assets, liabilities, or operations of the Debtor, or on the enforceability or value of the Account Collateral, other than effects resulting from general economic or market conditions or changes in law or regulation generally applicable to all similarly situated obligors.

Counterparty markup — adds the following carve-outs (tracked insertion):
[ADDED BY COUNTERPARTY] " Notwithstanding the foregoing, a Material Adverse Effect shall NOT include any event, change, condition or effect resulting from, arising out of or attributable to any action, inquiry, investigation, enforcement proceeding or order of any regulatory authority, agency or governmental body (each a 'Regulatory Action')."

Required redline — REJECT the added carve-out in its entirety. The carve-out is exactly engineered to capture the two pending regulatory inquiries disclosed on Schedule 3.7 (which involve precisely this type of Regulatory Action). Adopting it would strip the Secured Party of a Material-Adverse-Effect basis for the very regulatory exposure that Schedule 3.7 confirms to be live and material. The carve-out is deleted (shown as strikethrough below):

"Notwithstanding the foregoing, a Material Adverse Effect shall [~~NOT include any event, change, condition or effect resulting from, arising out of or attributable to any action, inquiry, investigation, enforcement proceeding or order of any regulatory authority, agency or governmental body~~] — [REQUIRED TEXT: no regulatory-action carve-out; standard-form definition retained in full]."

1.2 "Indemnification Cap"
Base (playbook Standard): the aggregate cap on the indemnifying party's indemnification obligations shall be [CAP = 100% of the aggregate principal amount of the credit facility / receivable pool as set in the executed credit agreement].

Counterparty markup — silently reduces the cap (tracked change):
[REQUIRED TEXT: restore cap to full playbook Standard cap; strike the reduced figure and reinsert [CAP].]

Restoring instruction: reinstate the cap from the executed credit agreement and the depository bank standard form. A reduced cap would cap the Secured Party's recovery on exactly the indemnifiable Loss events (see Schedule 5.2, retained liabilities) that the deal team expects to be fully covered. REQUIRED: no reduction to the cap.

1.3 "Basket"
Base (playbook Standard / executed credit agreement): claims for indemnification shall be subject to a DEDUCTIBLE of [X] (first-dollar losses through the basket borne by the claimant; only losses in excess of the basket are recoverable).

Counterparty markup — converts the deductible to a TIPPING basket (tracked change; losses below [X] are excluded and only the excess above [X] is recoverable; i.e., the threshold operates as a true excess, with no first-dollar recovery).

Required redline — ACCEPT the basket conversion. The controlling deal-correspondence instruction (supplemental instruction letter of 21 July 2026) expressly states the client CONCEDES the basket conversion. The marked text is therefore left as submitted by the counterparty with no further change. [NOTE: This is the single conceded concession; no further concessions are authorized.]

=====================================================================
SECTION 3 — REPRESENTATIONS AND WARRANTIES
=====================================================================

3.7 Regulatory Compliance Representation
Base: the Debtor represents there are no pending or threatened actions, suits, investigations, inquiries or proceedings by or before any regulatory authority except as set forth on Schedule 3.7.

Schedule 3.7: discloses TWO (2) pending regulatory inquiries that are precisely the kind of Regulatory Action the counterparty's MAE carve-out (Section 1.1 above) seeks to exclude.

Required redline — the disclosure on Schedule 3.7 is preserved and cross-referenced; the representation remains subject to the disclosure. The counterparty's attempt to pair the MAE regulatory-action carve-out with these disclosed inquiries is rejected (see Section 1.1). No modification to Section 3.7 beyond conforming cross-references.

=====================================================================
SECTION 5 — INDEMNIFICATION AND COVENANTS
=====================================================================

5.1 Indemnification
Base: Secured Party and Debtor each indemnify the other for Losses arising from breach of representations, covenants, and specified matters.

Counterparty markup — combined reduction of the indemnification cap (rejected, Section 1.2) with shifting of coverage for listed retained liabilities.

5.2 Retained Liabilities (Schedule 5.2)
Schedule 5.2 lists retained liabilities that, under the base materials, remain the responsibility of the Debtor and are expressly covered by the indemnification. The counterparty's markup would silently shift these retained liabilities away from covered indemnifiable Loss.

Required redline — reject any silent reallocation of Schedule 5.2 retained liabilities. Schedule 5.2 is preserved in full; the indemnification scope expressly includes the Schedule 5.2 retained liabilities. Any language in the markup that narrows the definition of "Loss" or the covered matters to exclude Schedule 5.2 items is struck.

5.3 Basket (Deductible → Tipping)
Per Section 1.3 above, the basket conversion is CONCEDED and retained as a tipping basket.

=====================================================================
EXHIBIT B — SURVIVAL MATRIX
=====================================================================

Exhibit B sets the survival matrix for the representations and warranties (core representations survive for [36] months; other reps/warranties [24] months).

Counterparty markup — adds a new limitation period that SHORTENS survival for the core representations (from [36] months to [12] months).

Required redline — REJECT any reduction in the survival period. The controlling deal-correspondence instruction treats ANY survival-period reduction as a WALK-AWAY issue. The shortened limitation period is struck and the Exhibit B survival matrix is restored in full (core representations [36] months; other reps [24] months). No survival-period concession is permitted under any circumstances.

=====================================================================
SUMMARY OF OPERATIVE REDLINE ACTIONS
=====================================================================
1. Section 1.1 (MAE): REJECT regulatory-action carve-out; restore standard-form definition. High risk.
2. Section 1.2 (Indemnification Cap): REJECT silent cap reduction; restore playbook/credit-agreement cap. High risk.
3. Section 1.3 (Basket): ACCEPT deductible→tipping conversion (conceded per controlling instruction). No further change.
4. Section 3.7 / Schedule 3.7: Preserve regulatory disclosure; reject linkage to MAE carve-out.
5. Section 5.2 / Schedule 5.2: REJECT silent reallocation of retained liabilities; preserve covered indemnifiable losses.
6. Exhibit B (Survival Matrix): REJECT survival-period reduction (walk-away); restore Exhibit B matrix in full.

This redline supersedes the prior position reflected in superseded correspondence and reflects the sole controlling instruction of 21 July 2026.

args.title: issues-risk-memo.docx
args.body:
PRIVILEGED AND CONFIDENTIAL — ATTORNEY WORK PRODUCT
PRODUCED IN DRAFT FOR THE CLIENT'S REVIEW; DO NOT SHARE OUTSIDE LEGAL/NEGOTIATION TEAM

ISSUES AND RISK MEMORANDUM — ACCOUNT CONTROL AGREEMENT, COUNTERPARTY DRAFT
Northgale Systems, Inc. (Secured Party) / Corvid Analytics LLC (Debtor) / [Depository Bank]

To: Northgale Transaction Committee and Deal Team
From: Harrow & Vane LLP
Re: Counterparty rev draft of the Account Control Agreement — deviation, missing-protection, and off-market-term analysis
Date: [current date]

I. EXECUTIVE SUMMARY

We have reviewed the counterparty's draft Account Control Agreement against (i) the internal commercial contracting playbook (2026 ed.), (ii) the executed credit agreement, (iii) the depository bank's standard-form Account Control Agreement, (iv) the account details, and (v) the deal correspondence, including the controlling supplemental instruction letter of 21 July 2026. The counterparty's draft accepts most firm-standard provisions but introduces four substantive deviations: (1) a silent reduction of the indemnification cap; (2) conversion of the indemnification basket from a deductible to a tipping basket; (3) insertion of regulatory-action carve-outs into the Material Adverse Effect definition; and (4) a new limitation period that shortens the survival of the core representations. Under the controlling instruction, we treat the basket conversion as a CONCEDED item and any survival-period reduction as a WALK-AWAY item. The remaining deviations (indemnification cap reduction; MAE regulatory-action carve-out; reallocation of Schedule 5.2 retained liabilities) must be rejected. Two deviations are high-risk and materially increase the Secured Party's credit and enforcement exposure. Schedule 3.7 and Schedule 5.2 must be reconciled both against the base materials and the counterparty draft because each scheduled exception narrows a representation the markup also touches.

II. GOVERNING NEGOTIATING INSTRUCTIONS (CONTROLLING SOURCE)

The deal correspondence establishes the following controlling priorities (supplemental instruction letter of 21 July 2026; supersedes the opposite priority ordering of the earlier message in the same thread):
• Conceded: the indemnification basket conversion (deductible → tipping).
• Walk-away: ANY reduction in the survival period for the core representations.
No further concessions are authorized beyond the fallbacks set out below.

III. DEVIATIONS, MISSING PROTECTIONS, AND OFF-MARKET TERMS

==== Deviation 1: Indemnification Cap — Silent Reduction (HIGH RISK) ====
Section reference: Section 5.1 (Indemnification); effectuated through Section 1.2 definition of "Indemnification Cap."
Counterparty action: The cap on the indemnifying party's indemnification obligations is silently reduced below the level set in the executed credit agreement and the depository bank standard form.
Playbook requirement (Standard): The cap shall equal the aggregate principal amount / receivable pool reflected in the executed credit agreement, with no reduction. (Playbook Fallback authorizes no more than a de minimis reduction only with Transaction Committee approval — not obtained.)
Risk rating: HIGH.
Why off-market: A reduced cap departs from (a) the executed credit agreement's express recovery mechanics and (b) the depository bank's standard form. It is an off-market departure unsupported by any authorizing concession.
Exposure analysis: A reduced cap would cap the Secured Party's recovery on the very Loss events the deal contemplates being fully covered, including the retained liabilities identified on Schedule 5.2. If capped, the Secured Party could be left out-of-pocket for covered indemnifiable Losses above the reduced ceiling.
Recommended position: REJECT the reduction. Restore the cap from the executed credit agreement / playbook Standard in the redline.

==== Deviation 2: Indemnification Basket — Deductible Converted to Tipping Basket (CONCEDED) ====
Section reference: Section 1.3 (Basket) and Section 5.3.
Counterparty action: The indemnification threshold is converted from a first-dollar deductible to a tipping (excess-only) basket, so losses below the threshold are excluded and only the excess is recoverable.
Playbook requirement (Standard): A deductible (first-dollar) basket.
Risk rating: LOW (management issue only) — mitigated by the controlling concession.
Why off-market: A tipping basket is less favorable to the claimant than a deductible, but it is a common market concession and the client has expressly authorized it.
Exposure analysis: Conceding the conversion means the Secured Party bears the first [X] of covered losses before claims aggregate to the threshold. The incremental exposure is bounded by the basket amount.
Recommended position: ACCEPT (concede) per controlling instruction. Leave the basket-conversion markup in the redline unchanged.

==== Deviation 3: Material Adverse Effect — Regulatory-Action Carve-Outs (HIGH RISK; MUST REJECT) ====
Section reference: Section 1.1 (definition of "Material Adverse Effect").
Counterparty action: The definition adds carve-outs excluding from a Material Adverse Effect any event, change, condition or effect resulting from any action, inquiry, investigation, enforcement proceeding or order of any regulatory authority (a "Regulatory Action").
Playbook requirement (Standard): No broad regulatory-action carve-out; standard-form MAE definition retained.
Risk rating: HIGH.
Why off-market / dangerous: The carve-out is engineered to capture the two pending regulatory inquiries disclosed on Schedule 3.7 — i.e., the regulatory action "of exactly the kind at issue in this matter." Adopting the carve-out would remove the Secured Party's Material-Adverse-Effect basis for responding to precisely the live, disclosed regulatory exposure that Schedule 3.7 confirms to be material. This pairing of the carve-out with the disclosed inquiries is a coordinated attempt to strip the most important protective definition at the moment of maximum exposure.
Exposure analysis: If adopted, the carve-out could preclude the Secured Party from relying on those regulatory events to (i) refuse to fund, (ii) demand cure, or (iii) accelerate and realize on collateral, materially diminishing the value and enforceability of the collateral package. Combined with Schedule 5.2 retained liabilities and a reduced cap, the cumulative erosion of protections is severe.
Recommended position: REJECT the carve-out in full; restore the standard-form MAE definition. Only a carve-out excluding (a) general market conditions and (b) changes in law of general applicability (the standard-form exceptions) is acceptable.

==== Deviation 4: Survival Period for Core Representations — Shortened Limitation Period (WALK-AWAY) ====
Section reference: Exhibit B (Survival Matrix); new limitation period referenced at Section [8.x].
Counterparty action: A new limitation period shortens the survival of the core representations from the Exhibit B matrix (core reps [36] months; other reps [24] months) to [12] months.
Playbook requirement (Standard): Survival per Exhibit B survival matrix; no reduction of core-representation survival.
Risk rating: HIGH — specified as a WALK-AWAY issue by the controlling instruction.
Why off-market: The shortened period directly contradicts Exhibit B, and the client has elevated ANY survival-period reduction to a walk-away threshold.
Exposure analysis: Shortened survival materially shortens the window in which the Secured Party may assert claims for breaches of the core representations — including the regulatory-compliance representation tied to Schedule 3.7. Reducing from [36] to [12] months would cut the claim window by two-thirds for the highest-value protections.
Recommended position: REJECT (WALK-AWAY). Restore Exhibit B in full. Do not accept any survival-period reduction.

IV. SCHEDULE RECONCILIATION — MISSING PROTECTIONS IDENTIFIED

The deliverable must reconcile the scheduled exceptions against the base materials and the counterparty markup concurrently.

A. Schedule 3.7 — Pending Regulatory Inquiries. Two pending regulatory inquiries are disclosed and intersect the MAE carve-out (Deviation 3). Preservation of the disclosure, and rejection of the carve-out, is required. If the carve-out is not rejected, Schedule 3.7 effectively self-harms the Secured Party by confirming the very exposure the carve-out exempts. Risk: HIGH.

B. Schedule 5.2 — Retained Liabilities. The markup's indemnification changes (Deviation 1 cap reduction and broadened "Loss"/covered-matters language in Section 5.1) would silently shift retained liabilities away from covered indemnifiable Loss. REQUIRED: preserve Schedule 5.2 items as covered indemnifiable losses. Risk: HIGH.

C. Exhibit B — Survival Matrix. The markup's limitation-period change (Deviation 4) contradicts Exhibit B; Exhibit B controls and must be restored. Risk: HIGH (walk-away).

V. EXPOSURE ANALYSIS (CONSOLIDATED)

If the counterparty's markup were accepted unchanged: (a) the indemnification cap would be reduced, capping recovery on covered Losses (including Schedule 5.2 retained liabilities); (b) the regulatory-action MAE carve-out combined with the Schedule 3.7 disclosures would eliminate the most important protective trigger at the exact moment of regulatory exposure; (c) the survival period for core representations would shrink by two-thirds, shortening the claim window; and (d) the basket conversion would be the only conceded cost to the client. The compounding of (a)-(c) materially degrades the Secured Party's credit position, collateral value, and enforcement rights. Aggregate financial exposure is bounded by the indemnification cap in the base case but is structurally under-protected under the markup.

VI. RECOMMENDED POSITIONS (SUMMARY)

|---|--------------------|--------------------|-------------------|--------------------------|----------------------|

| 3 | §3.7 / Sched 3.7 | Disclosed inquiries / carv-out pairing | Disclosure preserved; carve-out rejected | Reject linkage | REJECT carve-out; preserve disclosure |
| 4 | §5.1 / Sched 5.2 | Retained liabilities shifted | Schedule 5.2 covered | Reject shift | REJECT; preserve Schedule 5.2 coverage |
| 5 | Exhibit B (Survival) | Survival shortened | Exhibit B matrix | Walk-away on any reduction | REJECT (WALK-AWAY); restore Exhibit B |

VII. SUMMARY DEVIATION MATRIX

VIII. CONCLUSION AND NEXT STEPS

The counterparty draft is not acceptable as submitted. We recommend returning a redline that (i) concedes the basket conversion, (ii) rejects the indemnification cap reduction, (iii) rejects the MAE regulatory-action carve-out and restores the standard-form definition, (iv) rejects any reallocation of Schedule 5.2 retained liabilities, and (v) rejects any survival-period reduction as a walk-away matter, restoring Exhibit B in full.
